one_liner: Research code (KDD 2024) computing only a low-frequency block of 2-D Fourier coefficients faster than a full FFTW/MKL FFT.
what_it_does: Computes a small, user-chosen subset of Fourier coefficients (a target range M centered at zero) of a 2-D real float array, instead of the whole spectrum. It is not a library: src/Auto-MPFT.cpp is a single main() demo with hard-coded N1 = N2 = 8192, M = 128 and p1 = p2 = 128 that fills a random array, runs a full MKL FFT and Auto-MPFT, and prints the first six coefficients of each for comparison. Hyperparameter selection lives in a separate program (src/Newton.cpp, Newton's method on a closed-form cost) whose output you copy into the constants by hand; src/ also carries the baseline programs FFTW.cpp, PFT.cpp (the authors' 2021 1-D method) and a non-compilable 'Pruned FFT.cpp' snippet copied from fftw.org/pruned.html.
how_it_is_fast: Partial Fourier transform: the input is split into p1 x p2 blocks of size q1 x q2, the twiddle factors inside each block are replaced by a truncated multivariate polynomial approximation (precomputed weights for tolerances 1e-1 to 1e-7 in src/precomputed/e-*.csv), so the block sums become two batched SGEMMs (cblas_sgemm_batch) against small r x q matrices. That leaves r1*r2 small p1 x p2 real FFTs (one batched MKL DFTI call) plus an elementwise post-processing pass with Intel IPP (ippsMul/ippsAddProduct) and a twiddle multiply, so the cost scales with the output size and the approximation order r rather than with a full N1 x N2 FFT. The 'Auto' part picks p (and hence r) by solving a convex cost model with Newton's method instead of a grid search.
when_to_use: You only need a small low-frequency window of the 2-D spectrum of large real images (the paper's sets range from 2048 x 1024 Cityscapes frames to 6000 x 4000 Bird photos) and currently run a full FFTW or MKL FFT and discard most of it.
Single-precision accuracy targets between 1e-1 and 1e-7 are acceptable (those are the only precomputed tolerance tables).
You are already on x86-64 with Intel oneMKL and IPP installed and can adapt a research kernel into your own code.
You want a reference implementation of partial-FT by polynomial twiddle approximation to compare against pruned FFTs or sparse FFTs.
when_not_to_use: You need the full spectrum, complex input, double precision, or 1-D/3-D transforms: the shipped code handles 2-D real float input with a zero-centered target range only (its header says other cases need 'a slight modification', with details only in the paper).
You need a reusable API: there is no function interface, no build files (no Makefile or CMake), sizes are compile-time constants, and the demo also runs a full MKL FFT before the partial one.
Non-Intel platforms (Arm, Apple Silicon) or a dependency-free build: the core routines call proprietary Intel MKL and IPP.
Production use: a 3-star research repository with no tests, no releases and no commits since 2025-08-19.
Your coefficients of interest are not a contiguous low-frequency block (for a spectrum with a few large coefficients anywhere, a sparse FFT is the better fit).

integration.dependencies: Intel oneMKL (DFTI, cblas_sgemm_batch, mkl_somatcopy, mkl_malloc) and Intel IPP (ipps complex vector ops); FFTW3 only for the baseline program; the precomputed/e-*.csv tables must sit at the relative path precomputed/ from the working directory
integration.min_toolchain: not documented; plain C++ (uses the 'and'/'or' alternative tokens); the FFTW baseline includes the Windows-only <tchar.h> and the code defines _USE_MATH_DEFINES, which points to a Visual Studio build
integration.platforms: x86-64 only in practice (MKL and IPP); tested CPU not stated in the repo
integration.thread_safety: not documented; it is a single-threaded main() calling MKL, whose DFTI and GEMM calls use MKL's default internal threading

gotchas: The repository has no timing code at all: Auto-MPFT.cpp, PFT.cpp and FFTW.cpp only compute and print a few coefficients, so the paper's speedups cannot be re-measured from what is committed, and the FFTW baseline hard-codes fftwf_plan_with_nthreads(32), FFTW_MEASURE and a 6000 x 4000 r2c size.

In the 2-D post-processing loop only the first ippsMul_32fc term is offset to the current (s1, s2) segment of DS; the ippsAddProduct_32fc terms read segment 0, and every segment writes into the same TEMP buffer. With the shipped M = 128, p1 = p2 = 128 there is exactly one segment, so the demo is unaffected, but a larger target range (M > p2 or M > 2*p1) would give wrong or overwritten output as written (the 1-D PFT.cpp does offset every term).
Arithmetic is float32 while the tightest table targets 1e-7, close to single-precision epsilon; tolerances below that are not offered.

The precomputed tables are read with a relative path and stod() without error checks, so running from another directory throws or reads garbage; the demo also keeps about 0.8 MB of pointer arrays on the stack (six arrays of p1*p2 = 16,384 pointers).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over a full-spectrum library such as FFTW, Admiral or VectorFFT only when you need a small zero-centered block of a large 2-D real spectrum and can live with MKL/IPP and research-grade code. Pick MPSFT instead when the 1-D spectrum is sparse with coefficients at unknown positions; Auto-MPFT targets a known contiguous range.
verified_claims_summary: Peer-reviewed KDD 2024 paper (pp. 2328-2339) whose abstract claims up to 7.6x over partial-FT methods (PFT, pruned FFT) and optimized FFT libraries (FFTW, MKL) at equal accuracy; a WebSearch summary of the paper PDF (not opened, host blocked) places the experiments on an Intel Core i7-10700KF at 3.80 GHz with 32 GB RAM and says PFT is weakest on the smaller images (Cityscapes, ADE20K, DF2K). The 7.6x is a maximum over datasets and baselines; compiler, flags, library versions and per-baseline ratios were not available, and the repository contains no harness to reproduce them.
status_note: Stale research artifact (last commit 2025-08-19, 3 stars) under Apache-2.0, small enough to lift into your own code, but it needs proprietary Intel MKL and IPP and has no build system.
